# We implement a tiled matrix multiplication using shared memory and optimized loops.
# For simplicity, we use a straightforward element-wise approach but with fused operations:
# Since A is (M, K) and B is (K, N), result C = A @ B -> (M, N).

__global__ void matmul_kernel(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int M, int K, int N) {
    // Each block processes a tile of size BLOCK_M x BLOCK_K from A and BLOCK_K x BLOCK_N from B.
    // We'll use a simple approach: each thread computes one element of the output tile.
    // For simplicity, we implement a naive but fused matmul using loops over rows/cols.

    int col = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_N + threadIdx.x;

        float sum = 0.0f;

// Tiled matrix multiplication: each thread computes one output element C[i,j]
__global__ void matmul_tiled_kernel(const float* A, const float* B, float* C, int M, int K, int N) {
    // Each block handles a tile of rows (M/BLOCK_M x K) and columns (N/BLOCK_N x K)

    int col = blockIdx.x * BLOCK_N + threadIdx.x;

            int b_idx = k * N + col;

        }
        C[row * N + col] = sum;
    }

    int num_blocks_col = (N + BLOCK_N - 1) / BLOCK_N;
